lca.description: One row per H-1B Labor Condition Application (LCA) filed with the Department of Labor, FY2024 Q1 to FY2026 Q3, amendments deduplicated. An LCA is a filing an employer must make BEFORE an H-1B petition; it is not an approval or a visa.

columns.name: case_number
columns.description: DOL case number, unique per row.

columns.name: case_status
columns.description: DOL decision. Use 'CERTIFIED' for filings employers could actually use.

columns.name: fiscal_year
columns.description: US federal fiscal year of the decision (Oct 1 - Sep 30). FY2026 = Oct 2025 - Sep 2026.

columns.name: quarter
columns.description: Fiscal quarter 1-4 (Q1 = Oct-Dec).

columns.name: received_date
columns.description: Date DOL received the LCA.

columns.name: decision_date
columns.description: Date DOL decided the LCA.

columns.name: job_title
columns.description: Job title as typed by the employer (free text, messy). Do not filter on it: use role_family.

columns.name: title_norm
columns.description: Lowercased job title with abbreviations expanded (sr -> senior, ml -> machine learning).

columns.name: role_family
columns.description: Clean role category built offline from the title and SOC code. Get the value from find_role.

columns.name: seniority
columns.description: Seniority parsed from the title: intern, junior, mid, senior, staff_plus, manager or unspecified.

columns.name: soc_code
columns.description: Standard Occupational Classification code, e.g. 15-1252 = Software Developers.

columns.name: soc_title
columns.description: Name of the SOC occupation.

columns.name: full_time
columns.description: 'Y' if full-time.

columns.name: total_worker_positions
columns.description: Number of workers this one LCA covers. SUM it to count jobs; COUNT(*) counts filings.

columns.name: filing_type
columns.description: Why the LCA was filed. 'new_employment' is the closest proxy for a new (often lottery) hire; 'continuation' is an extension; 'change_employer' is a transfer.

columns.name: new_employment
columns.description: Workers in this filing who are new employment.

columns.name: continued_employment
columns.description: Workers who are continuing employment (extensions).

columns.name: change_employer
columns.description: Workers transferring from another employer.

columns.name: employer_id
columns.description: Resolved employer key: all legal-name variants of one company share it. Get it from find_employer.

columns.name: employer
columns.description: Canonical employer name (e.g. 'Google' for GOOGLE LLC, Google Inc.). Get it from find_employer.

columns.name: employer_type
columns.description: big_tech, finance, consulting, staffing_it_services, h1b_dependent, university or other. Universities are usually cap-exempt (no lottery).

columns.name: employer_name_raw
columns.description: Employer name exactly as filed. Do not filter on it: use employer_id.

columns.name: naics_code
columns.description: Employer's industry code (NAICS).

columns.name: worksite_city
columns.description: Normalized worksite city ('New York City' covers Manhattan, Brooklyn, NYC, ...).

columns.name: worksite_city_raw
columns.description: Worksite city as typed by the employer.

columns.name: worksite_county
columns.description: Worksite county as filed.

columns.name: worksite_state
columns.description: Two-letter worksite state.

columns.name: worksite_zip
columns.description: Five-digit worksite ZIP code.

columns.name: area_code
columns.description: OFLC wage area (metro) code for the worksite. Get it from find_location.

columns.name: metro_name
columns.description: OFLC wage area name, e.g. 'New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ'.

columns.name: wage_from_raw
columns.description: Offered wage as filed, in wage_unit (mixes hourly and yearly). Never aggregate it.

columns.name: wage_to_raw
columns.description: Top of the offered wage range as filed, in wage_unit, often blank.

columns.name: wage_unit
columns.description: Unit of the raw wage: Hour, Week, Bi-Weekly, Month or Year.

columns.name: wage_annual_from
columns.description: Offered wage converted to a yearly amount (Hour x 2080, Week x 52, Bi-Weekly x 26, Month x 12). Use this for pay.

columns.name: wage_annual_to
columns.description: Top of the offered range, yearly (equals wage_annual_from when no range).

columns.name: wage_flag
columns.description: 'ok' or why the wage is unreliable. Filter wage_flag = 'ok' for any pay statistic.

columns.name: pw_annual
columns.description: Prevailing wage the employer cited, yearly.

columns.name: pw_wage_level
columns.description: Wage level (I-IV) the EMPLOYER chose for the prevailing wage. Blank when a survey or union wage was used.

columns.name: pw_level_num
columns.description: pw_wage_level as a number 1-4.

columns.name: offer_wage_level
columns.description: Level (0-4) the OFFERED annual wage reaches in the 2026-27 OFLC table for this SOC and area; 0 = below Level I. Computed offline.

columns.name: h1b_dependent
columns.description: 'Y' if the employer declared itself H-1B dependent (a large share of its workforce is on H-1B).

columns.name: willful_violator
columns.description: 'Y' if DOL found the employer a willful violator.

columns.name: total_worksite_locations
columns.description: Number of worksites on the filing.

columns.name: source_file
columns.description: DOL file the row came from.

columns.name: offer_lottery_entries
columns.description: Lottery entries (1-4) this offer would get under the wage-weighted H-1B lottery, from offer_wage_level. Approximate: uses the 2026-27 wage table for all years.

columns.name: employer_id
columns.description: Employer key (joins lca.employer_id).

columns.name: employer
columns.description: Canonical name.

columns.name: employer_type
columns.description: See lca.employer_type.

columns.name: naics_code
columns.description: Most common NAICS code across its filings.

columns.name: filings
columns.description: Number of H-1B LCAs in the data.

columns.name: alias_count
columns.description: How many raw name spellings were merged into this employer.

columns.name: h1b_dependent_share
columns.description: Share of its filings marked H-1B dependent.

columns.name: aliases
columns.description: Up to 25 raw name spellings, most common first.

wage_levels.description: OFLC prevailing wage thresholds for wage year Jul 2026 - Jun 2027, annualized (hourly x 2080). One row per area x SOC code.

columns.name: area_code
columns.description: OFLC wage area code (joins lca.area_code).

columns.name: metro_name
columns.description: Area name.

columns.name: soc_code
columns.description: SOC code (joins lca.soc_code).

columns.name: soc_title
columns.description: SOC occupation name.

columns.name: level_1
columns.description: Level I (entry) annual wage.

columns.name: level_2
columns.description: Level II annual wage.

columns.name: level_3
columns.description: Level III annual wage.

columns.name: level_4
columns.description: Level IV (fully competent) annual wage.

columns.name: geo_level
columns.description: 1 = wage from this area's own data; higher = borrowed from a wider area.

areas.description: OFLC wage areas (metros and non-metro regions).

columns.name: area_code
columns.description: Area code.

columns.name: metro_name
columns.description: Area name.

columns.name: states
columns.description: States it covers.

columns.name: counties_or_towns
columns.description: Number of counties/towns in it.

role_titles_summary.description: Distinct normalized titles with their role family and filing counts. find_role searches this.

columns.name: title_norm
columns.description: Normalized title.

columns.name: role_family
columns.description: Role family.

columns.name: seniority
columns.description: Parsed seniority.

columns.name: filings
columns.description: Filings with this title.

petitions.description: USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub, FY2024 to FY2026: the FIRST DECISION U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services made on H-1B petitions (Form I-129), one row per employer and fiscal year. This is the step AFTER the LCA. Employer-level only: no role, salary, wage level or worksite. An approved petition is not yet a visa. FY2026 covers the full fiscal year (to Sep 30, 2026), while lca stops at FY2026 Q3.

columns.name: fiscal_year
columns.description: Fiscal year USCIS decided the petitions (Oct 1 - Sep 30). A petition is usually decided months after its LCA, often in the next fiscal year.

columns.name: employer_id
columns.description: Same key as lca.employer_id and employers.employer_id; NULL when the petitioner has no LCA in this database. Get it from find_employer.

columns.name: employer
columns.description: Canonical employer name (the lca name when matched, else the USCIS name).

columns.name: in_lca
columns.description: True when the petitioner was matched to an employer in lca.

columns.name: industry
columns.description: Employer's NAICS sector as USCIS reports it, e.g. '54 - Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services'.
enum_values: 21 - Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
53 - Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
56 - Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services

columns.name: name_variants
columns.description: How many USCIS petitioner spellings were merged into this row.

columns.name: new_employment_approved
columns.description: Approved petitions for NEW employment: first-time H-1B workers, mostly lottery (cap) winners plus cap-exempt hires. The closest count to 'new H-1B hires approved'.

columns.name: new_employment_denied
columns.description: Denied new-employment petitions.

columns.name: continuation_approved
columns.description: Approved extensions for workers continuing with the same employer.

columns.name: continuation_denied
columns.description: Denied extensions.

columns.name: change_same_employer_approved
columns.description: Approved petitions changing the job terms with the same employer.

columns.name: change_same_employer_denied
columns.description: Denied same-employer change petitions.

columns.name: new_concurrent_approved
columns.description: Approved petitions for a second, concurrent H-1B job.

columns.name: new_concurrent_denied
columns.description: Denied concurrent petitions.

columns.name: change_employer_approved
columns.description: Approved transfers: workers already in H-1B status moving to this employer.

columns.name: change_employer_denied
columns.description: Denied transfers.

columns.name: amended_approved
columns.description: Approved amended petitions.

columns.name: amended_denied
columns.description: Denied amended petitions.

columns.name: approved
columns.description: All approved petitions that year (sum of the six *_approved columns).

columns.name: denied
columns.description: All denied petitions that year (sum of the six *_denied columns).

glossary.LCA: Labor Condition Application: the employer's wage attestation to the Department of Labor, filed before an H-1B petition. Certified LCA != approved petition != visa. Many LCAs are never used.
glossary.petition: Form I-129, filed with USCIS after the LCA is certified. The `petitions` table has USCIS's first decisions (approved or denied) per employer and fiscal year. Pipeline: LCA (DOL) -> lottery registration (new cap-subject hires only) -> petition (USCIS) -> visa (State Department). Approval rate = approved / (approved + denied).
glossary.LCAs vs petitions: Employers file far more LCAs than petitions: one worker can need several LCAs (new worksite, amendment, extension), and many LCAs are never used. Compare the two as a ratio per employer, and say that fiscal years do not line up exactly.
glossary.wage level: OFLC sets four prevailing-wage levels per occupation and area: Level I (entry) to Level IV (fully competent).
glossary.wage-weighted lottery: Since the DHS rule effective Feb 27, 2026 (FY2027 cap season onward), each H-1B registration is entered once per wage level of the offered wage: Level I = 1 entry, II = 2, III = 3, IV = 4. Higher-paid offers have proportionally better odds.
glossary.lottery entries: offer_lottery_entries: 1-4, from the level the offered wage reaches in the OFLC table. 0 means the wage is below Level I.
glossary.cap-exempt: Universities, their affiliated nonprofits and nonprofit/government research organizations can sponsor H-1Bs without the lottery.
glossary.fiscal year: Oct 1 - Sep 30. FY2026 Q3 ends June 30, 2026 (the last data in this database).
glossary.H-1B dependent: An employer with a large share of H-1B workers; must make extra attestations. Common among IT staffing/outsourcing firms.
glossary.filings vs workers: COUNT(*) counts LCAs; SUM(total_worker_positions) counts positions.

join_hints: petitions.employer_id = lca.employer_id (aggregate lca per employer_id and fiscal_year BEFORE joining: petitions has one row per employer-year)
limitations: Who won the lottery or was issued a visa. (Approved and denied PETITIONS per employer and fiscal year ARE available, in `petitions`.)
Petition approvals or denials for a specific role, salary, wage level or city: `petitions` is employer-level only.
Salaries actually paid: LCAs show the wage offered on the filing.
Anything about an individual person, interview odds, offer rates or green-card (PERM) sponsorship.
LCA filings after FY2026 Q3 (June 30, 2026), petition decisions after FY2026 (Sep 30, 2026), or anything before FY2024.
Whether the $100,000 H-1B fee applies to a specific case, or immigration/legal advice.
Exact selection probability: entries are known, but the total pool of registrations by level is not in this data.

example_queries.question: Median offered pay and filing count for one employer's role family, by fiscal year
example_queries.sql: SELECT fiscal_year, median(wage_annual_from) AS median_pay, count(*) AS filings FROM lca WHERE employer_id = 42 AND role_family = 'Data Engineer' AND case_status = 'CERTIFIED' AND wage_flag = 'ok' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

example_queries.question: Share of an employer's new-employment filings at each employer-chosen wage level
example_queries.sql: SELECT pw_wage_level, count(*) AS filings, round(100.0 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct FROM lca WHERE employer_id = 42 AND filing_type = 'new_employment' AND case_status = 'CERTIFIED' AND pw_wage_level IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

example_queries.question: Top employers by worker positions in a metro for a role family
example_queries.sql: SELECT employer, sum(total_worker_positions) AS positions, count(*) AS filings FROM lca WHERE area_code = '12060' AND role_family = 'Software Engineer' AND case_status = 'CERTIFIED' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY positions DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.question: Average lottery entries for offers by employer type
example_queries.sql: SELECT employer_type, round(avg(offer_lottery_entries), 2) AS avg_entries, count(*) AS filings FROM lca WHERE case_status = 'CERTIFIED' AND offer_lottery_entries > 0 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY avg_entries DESC

example_queries.question: One employer's petition approvals, denials and approval rate by fiscal year
example_queries.sql: SELECT fiscal_year, new_employment_approved, new_employment_denied, approved, denied, round(100.0 * approved / nullif(approved + denied, 0), 1) AS approval_pct FROM petitions WHERE employer_id = 42 ORDER BY 1

example_queries.question: Certified new-employment LCA positions per approved new-employment petition, for one employer and year
example_queries.sql: WITH f AS (SELECT employer_id, sum(new_employment) AS lca_new_positions FROM lca WHERE employer_id = 42 AND fiscal_year = 2025 AND case_status = 'CERTIFIED' GROUP BY 1) SELECT p.employer, f.lca_new_positions, p.new_employment_approved, round(f.lca_new_positions / nullif(p.new_employment_approved, 0), 1) AS lca_positions_per_approval FROM petitions p JOIN f USING (employer_id) WHERE p.fiscal_year = 2025
